cicada.violet-marks.text: Small deep-violet marks, always the same shade, appear at head height on walls where crowds stand and wait: queues, tram stops, waiting rooms.

deputy-director.hears-refusals.text: The Deputy Director hears every refused order from a new intake himself, the same day, in his office.

deputy-director.name.text: The Deputy Director is called Seiichi Takamine. His printed signature, on every acceptance letter, is too hurried to read.

directorate.alarm-never-real.text: In a hundred and fifty years, the Directorate's alarm has never once been real.

directorate.answers-to-itself.text: The Directorate recruits separately from Minkai's army and navy, and operates outside Minkai's national lines.

directorate.base.text: The Directorate's base is its own man-made island in the harbour, built up around a rock and reached by a long causeway with a railway line beside it. A flat grey fortress with no windows stands at its southern end, among hangars, workshops, offices and barracks, and a high fence runs round the whole island.

directorate.brought-forward-stamp.text: Every candidate's acceptance letter this year has its printed reporting date ruled through, "Monday next" written beside it in pen, and a red BROUGHT FORWARD stamp. Nothing on intake day explains it.

directorate.brought-wealth.text: Not everyone trusts the Directorate, but few can argue against the vast wealth and technology it has brought to the area in so little time.

directorate.came-to-kurose.text: About a hundred and fifty years ago, the Directorate crossed the world and settled in Kurose.

directorate.curfew-minor.text: Breaking curfew is a very minor offence: it is written down, and the candidate is told off.

directorate.digs.text: The Directorate is Golarion's foremost gatherer of alien technology. It digs for it and locks it in deep storage vaults, so that it can't cause another disaster.

directorate.form-12b.text: Form 12-B, the intake screening form, asks for mother's maiden name twice: in box 4, and again in box 19, in capitals.

directorate.forms-typed-ahead.text: Every candidate's Form 12-B is typed with their name before they arrive, on the same admissions typewriter as their acceptance letter. Its lower-case e strikes low and faint.

directorate.founded-after.text: About five years after the rift, four of the people who had stood in front of it founded the Directorate, so that the response next time would be faster and more decisive.

directorate.free-time.text: A candidate's free time is theirs to choose: the gymnasium, the range, the library, or a lesson they pick themselves.

directorate.gate.text: At the land end of the causeway is the gate: a red-and-white barrier across the road, a guard booth not much bigger than a telephone box, and a guard with a ledger.

directorate.how-trainees-come.text: Some trainees volunteer, some are encouraged into it, and some are pushed into it.

directorate.intake-size.text: This year's intake is about forty candidates. The whole base turns out in the drill hall to welcome it.

directorate.missing-pilot-search.text: On intake morning, staff are quietly hunting for a pilot who hasn't turned up. A careful listener can catch the name Nozomi.

directorate.newcomers.text: Hundreds of people from across Golarion moved to Kurose to be part of the Directorate.

directorate.newcomers-built.text: The newcomers were engineers, clerks, scholars and pilots, and then the people who fed, housed and sold to them. They built streets and temples of their own.

directorate.no-track.text: Every candidate's section card names a track as well as a section. The six Section Nine cards leave the track blank, and so does the clerk's list.

directorate.on-report.text: A refused order goes on the candidate's file, and they are on report. If they are later proven right, that goes on the file too, in the Deputy Director's hand.

directorate.orders-serious.text: Refusing a direct order is the most serious thing a candidate can do. It means a hearing in front of someone senior, to explain themselves.

directorate.public-view.text: Kurose sees the Directorate as both a grand mission against a disaster nobody expects to see and a heavy-work corps everybody relies on, and people joke about the gap.

directorate.school-and-service.text: The Directorate is a school and a service at once: candidates sit lessons, and they also drill, carry orders and stand watches.

directorate.section-nine.text: The six are Section Nine. Each of them was told, alone, that their screen came back irregular.

directorate.sends-for-trainees.text: Every year the Directorate sends for new trainees.

directorate.trainee-expectations.text: Most people expect a spell as a trainee to be a faff and a bother: a duty which, once discharged, is done.

directorate.vials-to-medical.text: A requisition for a vial goes up to Medical for its countersignature: vials are Medical's.

directorate.warmongers.text: The Directorate is a foreign army in the harbour: intruders, outsiders, even warmongers.

directorate.who-joins.text: People apply to the Directorate, or are streamed on to it from school.

directorate.why-kurose-unexplained.text: The Directorate has never said publicly why it believes there will be another rift, or why it crossed the world to wait for it in a fishing village.

era.engines.text: Magic is still part of everyday life, small and cheap, but the great works of this age are built with engines: steam and oil, then electricity; railways across continents, steamships that don't wait for the wind, and wires carrying voices between cities.

era.two-hundred-years.text: The rift at Kortos was about two hundred years ago, and the passage of time has changed much.

founders.charter-signatures.text: The founding charter carries four signatures: a flowing hand, a quick doctor's scrawl, HYUCK in capitals pressed so hard the nib tore the paper, and small careful characters in a script nobody in Kurose reads.

founders.names.text: The four are Hyuck, Rupiah, Anabala and Shucks Mordant.

founders.not-waved-about.text: The city doesn't make a fuss of its founders being long-lived. It's faintly embarrassing, so nobody waves it in anyone's face.

founders.painting.text: On Founding Day there is a painting of the four in some supporters' shop windows.

founders.pictures.text: Every approved picture of the four shows four tall, handsome humans.

founders.promise.text: They promised that the next time, nobody would be caught unprepared, and founded the Directorate to keep that promise.

founders.ribbon.text: At least one of the founders might turn up to cut the ribbon at a major event.

frames.clumsy.text: Frames are clumsy. One trying to step over a tram doesn't quite manage it.

frames.directorate-runs-them.text: The Directorate builds its Frames, crews them and keeps them running.

frames.look.text: A Frame is shaped roughly like a person and is taller than the warehouses it works beside. The pilot sits inside and works its arms and legs. Frames are patched, riveted and loud.

frames.mechanical.text: Frames are purely mechanical: clanking machines, hard work to drive.

frames.what-a-frame-is.text: A Frame is a mech: a walking machine with a pilot inside it.

frames.what-people-see.text: Every child in Kurose can tell you the Directorate was built to save the world, but the only thing anyone has ever seen a Frame do is lift girders at a building site or help lift a crate of cabbage.

glamour.aliens-outsiders.text: Aliens are treated as outsiders in Minkai.

glamour.cheap.text: Magic that lets someone disguise an unusual appearance is cheap and everywhere: glamoured clothes are sold on the high street.

glamour.debate.text: Anyone who looks too unusual for the neighbours tends to wear a glamour in public. Some call that good manners; some say easy disguise has pushed unusual-looking people into hiding when they have done nothing wrong.

glamour.refusers.text: Many aliens in the city refuse to disguise or tone down their appearance for anyone, and draw stares when they go out.

hyuck.statue.text: A weathered statue of a gnoll stands on the harbour with HYUCK on its plaque. People take it for somebody's mascot, since every picture of Hyuck shows a tall man with a sword.

kurose.everyday.text: Kurose has electric light in most of its streets, a radio in most kitchens, trams that run on time, and factories that work through the night.

kurose.far-east.text: Kurose is in Golarion's far east, on the far side of the world from Kortos.

kurose.first-families-stayed.text: The families who were there first still live in the old town.

kurose.fishing-village.text: About a hundred and fifty years ago, Kurose was a tiny fishing village with one road in.

kurose.grew-fast.text: The Directorate's money, harbour works and Frames turned the village into a great city within a few generations.

kurose.isolationists.text: Isolationist groups in Kurose are unhappy with what they see as a foreign thorn in their country's side. There is plenty of unrest among the city's groups.

kurose.left-behind.text: The change came so fast that it made winners and losers.

kurose.locals-and-newcomers.text: There is unrest between the families who lived in Kurose first and the hundreds of people from across Golarion who moved there to be part of the Directorate.

kurose.modern.text: The Directorate brought electricity and rapid, destabilising modernisation to Kurose in very little time.

kurose.old-town.text: The old town is on the waterfront, where the fishing village was.

kurose.organised-crime.text: Organised crime is a serious problem in Kurose.

kurose.shape.text: From above: a long bay with a beach and the city spread along it, a river through the middle with the tram lines following it inland, factories and smokestacks along the shore, and hills behind.

kurose.winners-and-losers.text: Some of the families who were there first did very well out of the Directorate. Some sold their land too cheaply and never forgave anybody.

manako.came-back-empty-handed.text: He came back from that errand empty-handed and was laughed at, and he has spent years going over what he should have done.

manako.chemist.text: Manako was a chemist for the Directorate, decades ago, and as a junior he was sent on the same errand the party gets.

manako.disgraced.text: He is the Directorate scientist who had a "breakdown" at a science conference, caused a huge fuss, and was expelled.

manako.district.text: Manako's tea house is in a district of the city where he has a lot of influence.

manako.name.text: The old man who owns the tea house is Manako, and he gives his name freely.

manako.the-vial-plan.text: His plan: take the docket at its word and requisition a replacement vial, a real and expensive part, which needs a countersignature from a desk above the sender's and makes a form saying who asked, and why.

minkai.can-defend-itself.text: Minkai feels it can more than defend itself.

minkai.grumbles.text: The Directorate operating outside Minkai's national lines grates on its army and navy, and they complain about a foreign base in their harbour.

minkai.own-forces.text: Minkai has its own army and navy. National service in them is what everyone's parents did.

nobu.off-book.text: Some of what Nobu hands out isn't Directorate stock. He buys it for cash from the ships' chandlers on the old town's waterfront, because issue never arrives on time.

rift.converged.text: Adventurers and magic-users converged to contain it, from across the island and then the whole region, among them the finest of Kortos's neighbouring states.

rift.four-at-the-end.text: Four people stood in front of it at the end.

rift.grew.text: It grew on whatever was near it: slowly at first, then faster, the rate itself slowly climbing, in fits and starts that made it deadly to study.

rift.histories-skip-the-start.text: The histories go from nothing to catastrophe and never say how it began.

rift.looked.text: It was a violet light with a black heart.

rift.nobody-knows-how.text: Nobody agreed on what it was, or why it happened.

rift.opened.text: About two hundred years ago, on the far side of the world, something opened in the air above the island of Kortos, near Absalom, and would not close.

rift.path.text: It carved a jagged path across the island towards Absalom, changing direction seemingly at random.

rift.swallowed.text: It absorbed many powerful priests, wizards and sorcerers who tried to stop it.

rift.uncertain-ending.text: It was forced back and crushed into a small space, and either destroyed or changed into something else. Nobody who was there ever confirmed which.

rupiah.cuts-the-ribbon.text: Rupiah is the founder who usually cuts the Founding Day ribbon.

school-history-teacher.name.text: The history teacher, who also takes local studies, is called Ota.

section-officer.the-docket.text: On their first afternoon, Vetch sends Section Nine into the city with a stores docket for COMPOUND, LEVELLING, BUBBLE, ONE (1): the bubble in a spirit level.

section-officer.the-drains.text: At supper on the first day, Vetch reads Section Nine the night's worst job in front of the hall: storm drain clearance under the old town, from Dock C at twenty-one hundred.

section-officer.the-job.text: At Dock C, Vetch gives them the job in one line: power to the drainage line, clear the compactor feed, report to him when it runs. He waits for them at the top.

section-officer.vetch.text: Section Officer Vetch runs Section Nine. He is never wrong in his own account.

shinobu.the-phone-in.text: On an evening radio phone-in, a father tries hard not to shout: his seventeen-year-old daughter is being held without charge, and nobody will tell him where. Neither of them is named on air.

shucks.hand-wandered.text: Asked about his right hand, Shucks says it wandered off. He means it, and it sounds like a joke.

shucks.head-of-medical.text: Shucks Mordant is the Directorate's head of medical.

shucks.rand-signature.text: When Section Nine climb out of the drains, Vetch is holding their vial requisition, countersigned in green ink over Medical's stamp: Rand, Medical. Nobody called Rand works in Medical; he has asked.

shucks.revealed-early.text: Shucks is the one founder the players meet at once: he runs their medical, and his badge says MORDANT.

visual-language.candidate-tunic.text: A candidate's uniform is a slate teal-grey tunic with a high collar and brass buttons, worn over a cream shirt, with a small orange tab on the collar.
